I used to lurk on Reddit, I rarely posted. I don't like posting, usually, because it puts my mind into an addictive loop of check-re-check. But I do like the exchange of ideas. But not really in person--it makes me feel like a windbag.

I don't expect anyone to read any of this. It is probably contradictory nonsense. I do want to try to be honest.

I am a male, nearly 40, white, a teacher. Married, with kids. I hope to have many. I pray to do a good job.

I am a mostly a traditionalist, meaning I usually like things that are organic or old, and I usually distrust things that are synthetic or novel. Usually, though not universally.

I am Catholic. Yes, Crusades, Galileo etc etc. I know more than you about the historical and current failings of Catholics. I like bells and smells and chanting and strange semi-pagan customs and a healthy sense of guilt and unworthiness in the face of God's love. I dislike most of the post-Vatican II innovations--they strike me as tacky horseshit at best, ungodly at worst.

I like to study other religions. I think some have some bits of truth, beauty, and goodness; I think they're mostly false. I think Hinduism looks like a good time. I think Islam is brutal at heart. Islamic art is magnificent. Muslims are the most hospitable people I've ever met. Protestantism is a tragedy and a fun-kill, and probably responsible for both the prudishness and lewdness of American sexuality. But I can sympathize with young Martin Luther. I sometimes wish I were Eastern Orthodox.

I dislike atheists of the Dawkins-type. They are frequently juvenile, uninformed, unfair, and condescending. Dawkin's "The Selfish Gene" was a brilliant and amazing book, I wonder if it is true. Old-school atheists of the Nietzsche stripe seem honest, though wrong. Atheism is plausible to me, but only when I feel down.

If Elon Musk or someone competent like that were to solicit donations for a Hubble 2.0, I would give $1000 immediately and as much as I could reasonably spare after that.

I like, or rather trust, ideas of region, religion, tribe/family, person, sex. I distrust ideas of nationality, ideology, race, citizen(consumer!), gender. Politics in general is gross. Republicans seem stupid and avaricious; Democrats seem evil and totalitarian. Libertarianism seems interesting but unworkable.

"Medicinal marijuana" is a sham. Marijuana should be legal. I'm not sure about the other drugs.

Abortion is the killing of a human, that seems scientifically self-evident. I can understand why women would want to do that in some situations.

Children need a mother and father. Divorce is usually selfish and horrid. I am a teacher, I see the effects on children.

Homosexuality is probably genetic. It is also disordered. The positive contributions of homosexuals to art, culture, and science are many.

I am probably racist, under the current academic definition. I think European culture is objectively more accomplished than others. I recognize that Europeans have done evil things--I don't think anyone else would have done any better under the same circumstances. I don't really like hanging out with most white people. Individually I think minorities are typically nicer to be around, though I wonder what is going on with their societies. If I were black, I would probably be pretty angry and militant. I don't hate anyone. I think white privilege is a real thing.

Towards men, women at worst are vindictive, manipulative, bird-brained nags. Towards women, men at worst are unhinged, violent monsters. Men, collectively, are the worse by far. At their best--each sex is a gift to the other.

I think there is such a thing as high and low art, though the difference isn't always clear. I love some of both. High art is more worthwhile. I love graffiti. I hate most modern art. I wish I knew ancient poetry--Latin, Greek, Hebrew, Sanskrit, Farsi, Japanese,classical Chinese, etc. I used to like electronic music more; I still love synthesizers. I mostly listen to funk and soul--lately, Brazillian 70s stuff. I love Bach. I love James Brown. I love Horace Silver. I love Steely Dan, though I'm not sure why. Kendrick Lamar's new album is probably the album of the decade. Other stuff: I love Moebius and weirdo comic books. I love A Canticle for Liebowitz. I love Herman Melville. I love Ozu. I love Kurosawa. I love Kubrick.

I like and use open-source software, even though much of it is janky.

I wish I knew more about sports, but I just can't really get into them. Same thing with video games.

I like Dungeon World. D&D feels like doing too much homework. I like board games, but my attention span doesn't cooperate. I can't afford Magic.

I love capoeira, though sadly I don't do it any more. I still love to dance. I like to make music--stupid techno and house mostly.

I like calligraphy, I'm ok.

Oh, I have alopecia totalis.
